subject: Biology
title: Human Skeletal System Architecture: Axial Skeleton (80 Bones)
learningObjectives: Identify the 80 bones of the Axial Skeleton across the Skull, Vertebral Column, and Thoracic Cage
Describe the anatomy of the dicondylic skull, Atlas (C1), and Axis (C2)
Classify True (1–7), False (8–10), and Floating (11–12) ribs
content:
The adult human skeleton consists of **206 Bones**, divided into the **Axial Skeleton (80 bones)** and the **Appendicular Skeleton (126 bones)**.

```
                          AXIAL SKELETON BREAKDOWN (80 Bones)
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
  SKULL (22 + 7 = 29)            VERTEBRAL COLUMN (26)           THORACIC CAGE (25)
  ├── Cranial Bones (8)          ├── Cervical (C₇)               ├── Sternum (1)
  ├── Facial Bones (14)          ├── Thoracic (T₁₂)              └── Ribs (24 = 12 pairs)
  ├── Hyoid Bone (1)             ├── Lumbar (L₅)                    ├── True (1–7)
  └── Auditory Ossicles (6)      ├── Sacral (S₍₅₎→₁)                ├── False (8–10)
      (Malleus, Incus, Stapes)   └── Coccygeal (Co₍₄₎→₁)            └── Floating (11–12)
```

### 6.1 Regional Anatomy of the Axial Skeleton

1. **The Skull (29 Bones)**:
   - **Cranial Bones (8)**: Frontal (1), Parietal (2), Temporal (2), Occipital (1), Sphenoid (1 butterfly-shaped bone forming cranial floor), Ethmoid (1).
   - **Facial Bones (14)**: Nasal (2), Maxillae (2), Zygomatic (2 cheek bones), Lacrimal (2), Palatine (2), Inferior Conchae (2), Vomer (1), Mandible (1 lower jaw - only movable skull bone).
   - **Dicondylic Articulation**: Features **2 Occipital Condyles** that articulate with the superior articular facets of the Atlas vertebra.
   - **Associated Bones (7)**: Single U-shaped **Hyoid Bone (1)** in the floor of the buccal cavity + **6 Auditory Ossicles** (Malleus, Incus, Stapes).
2. **The Vertebral Column (26 Bones)**:
   - Formula: $\mathbf{\text{C}_7\ \text{T}_{12}\ \text{L}_5\ \text{S}_{(5)\rightarrow 1}\ \text{Co}_{(4)\rightarrow 1} = 26\text{ Vertebrae}}$.
   - **Atlas ($\text{C}_1$)**: Lacks vertebral body and spinous process; forms atlanto-occipital condyloid joint for "Yes" nodding.
   - **Axis ($\text{C}_2$)**: Possesses vertical **Odontoid Process (Dens)** fitting into Atlas to form pivot joint for "No" rotation.
3. **Thoracic Cage & Ribs (25 Bones)**:
   - **Sternum (1)**: Flat ventral breastbone consisting of Manubrium, Body, and Xiphoid process.
   - **Ribs (12 Pairs = 24 Bones)**: Bicephalic (possessing Capitulum and Tuberculum dorsal facets):
     - **True Ribs (1st to 7th pairs)**: Vertebrosternal ribs; attach dorsally to thoracic vertebrae and ventrally directly to sternum via hyaline costal cartilage.
     - **False Ribs (8th, 9th, 10th pairs)**: Vertebrochondral ribs; join the costal cartilage of the 7th rib instead of articulating directly with the sternum.
     - **Floating Ribs (11th and 12th pairs)**: Vertebral ribs; remain unattached ventrally, protecting the retroperitoneal kidneys.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Evolutionary Origin of Auditory Ossicles
conceptBreakdown.explanation: In mammalian evolution, lower jaw bones migrated to the middle ear: (1) Malleus is derived from the reptilian Articular bone, (2) Incus is derived from the Quadrate bone, and (3) Stapes is derived from the Hyomandibular.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Bicephalic Nature of Ribs
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Human ribs have two articulation points on their posterior end: the Capitulum (head) articulates with the demifacet on the vertebral body, and the Tuberculum articulates with the facet on the transverse process of the thoracic vertebra.
